subject: Arteta bans Arsenal players from picking themselves in FPL after team news leaked via a squad member's team
title: Arteta bans self-picks in Fantasy Premier League

lines.vo: Christos Tzolis picked himself in fantasy football. Then he made himself captain.
lines.footage: Tzolis goal clip, Arsenal home match, then fantasy team screen graphic

lines.vo: Arteta has now banned Arsenal players from picking themselves in Fantasy Premier League. First rule of voting: not for yourself.
lines.footage: Arteta press conference clip, arms crossed, touchline

lines.vo: Tzolis picked and captained himself before the Liverpool game. That hinted he would start. Fantasy football just became team news.
lines.footage: Tzolis warm-up clip, Arsenal training ground

lines.vo: A week later, he moved himself, Ezri Konsa and Riccardo Calafiori out of his team. Captain one week, dropped the next.
lines.footage: Konsa and Calafiori match clips, Arsenal defensive line

lines.vo: Arteta says the leaks must stop, because confidentiality is what builds trust.
It is not just Arsenal. Chelsea warned staff too, after people moved one of their players out of fantasy teams.
lines.footage: Chelsea training clip, staff area, Stamford Bridge exterior

lines.vo: Want the next story before it breaks? Match news and betting tips at aboutfootball dot UK.

footage_terms: Arteta press conference Fantasy Premier League

inserts.story: A caricature Tzolis stands before a huge fantasy-team screen and clicks Captain on his own face. A giant armband slams onto his arm and drags him into the screen. Twist: the armband reads Banned, and a caricature Arteta calmly peels it off him.
inserts.characters: caricature Tzolis; generic round-headed fantasy manager

inserts.story: A team sheet pinned to a board has three cartoon players waving at the camera. The board flips and they all fall off. Twist: a caricature Arteta catches the sheet, shouts Confidential and swallows it.
inserts.characters: generic cartoon players; caricature Arteta; stylised board

inserts.story: A caricature Arteta locks a team sheet in a padlocked box. The key is a fantasy tracker with a cartoon face, which crawls out and picks itself. Twist: it captains itself.
inserts.characters: caricature Arteta; stylised padlock box; cartoon tracker character

facts_used: Christos Tzolis picked and captained himself in Fantasy Premier League before the Liverpool match, which signalled he had recovered (news id 61, espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/50539955)
The next week he transferred himself, Ezri Konsa and Riccardo Calafiori out of his team (news id 61)
Arteta said Arsenal have taken steps to stop leaks and players will no longer select themselves (news id 61)
Chelsea issued a similar warning to staff after Joao Pedro was dropped from FPL teams (news id 61)
notes: Comic (looney_slapstick). Chelsea's Joao Pedro injury context in the source is deliberately left out, and so is the 'recovered' angle on Tzolis; the script says only that he hinted he would start. Self-transfer detail is from the source's second fact. Stamford Bridge footage is only an idea; verify before use.
